# Appeal of Denial — Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)

**Rowan Carter**
[Street Address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Aetna — Member Complaint and Appeal Unit
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Fax: 859-425-3379

**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination**
- **Member name:** Rowan Carter
- **Member ID:** W914903090
- **Reference number:** POC-5BA41AD17E-24277
- **Date of denial notice:** August 19, 2026
- **Service denied:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
- **Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0660 – Knee Arthroplasty (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html)

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446). The notice dated August 19, 2026 states that the request does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision, because the plan's own published criteria in **Aetna CPB 0660 – Knee Arthroplasty** describe the situation my medical records document. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is needed.

Below I have set out the plan's own language next to what is in my chart.

## 1. The plan covers partial knee replacement when one compartment is affected — my records show one compartment

The plan's policy states:

> "Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty using Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved devices is considered medically necessary for members with advanced osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee affecting only a single compartment (medial, lateral or patellofemoral), and who meet the following criteria (see also Additional Note ):"

The policy also states:

> "unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is indicated when only 1 compartment is affected, and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is indicated when 2 or 3 compartments are affected."

My records establish disease in a single compartment. The MRI of my knee dated June 9, 2026 shows full-thickness cartilage loss in the **medial** compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence **grade 4 medially**. That is advanced osteoarthritis confined to one compartment — exactly the situation the policy identifies as the indication for a partial (unicompartmental) replacement rather than a total replacement.

## 2. The plan requires a history of failed conservative care — my records document 14 weeks, including formal physical therapy

The plan's policy requires:

> "and History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management;"

and specifies:

> "Members with osteoarthritis, traumatic arthritis, or avascular necrosis should have at least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (at least 24 weeks for persons with a relative contraindication) - with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) in the past year, including all of the following, unless contraindicated:"

My records establish this:

- **Supervised, in-person physical therapy:** 14 weeks, from April 10, 2026 to July 17, 2026, with 16 visits completed, focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This exceeds the 12-week minimum, and all 14 weeks were formal physical therapy with a licensed physical therapist — well over the "at least half" the policy asks for, and within the past year.
- **Medication:** NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** a corticosteroid injection on June 17, 2026, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- **Duration and severity:** 9 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest.

Conservative care was not skipped. It was tried, documented, and it did not work.

## 3. Pain and functional disability are documented

My records describe the functional impact in specific terms: I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake 3–4 times nightly with pain. On examination there was positive provocative testing on the affected side, and my range of motion is limited by pain.

## 4. Contraindications

The plan's policy states:

> "Total joint replacement is considered not medically necessary in persons with any of the following absolute contraindications:"

My records document no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

The policy also lists, among its criteria:

> "or Corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of the planned arthroplasty;"

My corticosteroid injection was given on **June 17, 2026**. The surgery has not yet been scheduled, and my surgeon can confirm a surgical date of [planned date of surgery] so that this timing element of the policy is satisfied. If timing is the concern behind the denial, I ask that it be addressed as a scheduling matter rather than as a basis for refusing coverage of the procedure itself.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Aetna to overturn the denial and authorize the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) as requested by Dr. Marchetti. The plan's policy states that unicompartmental knee arthroplasty is medically necessary for advanced osteoarthritis affecting only a single compartment in a member with a documented history of unsuccessful conservative therapy of at least 12 weeks, at least half of it formal in-person physical therapy. My records establish single-compartment, bone-on-bone, Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medial disease; 14 weeks and 16 visits of supervised physical therapy; 8 months of NSAIDs; a corticosteroid injection with only 2 weeks of partial relief; and daily functional limitation.

If any part of my record is considered incomplete, I ask that you tell me specifically which criterion in CPB 0660 you believe is unmet and what documentation would resolve it, so my surgeon's office can supply it promptly. I also request a copy of the clinical criteria and the reviewer's rationale used in this determination, and that the appeal be reviewed by a physician with expertise in orthopedic surgery.

I understand that my appeal must be received by **February 15, 2027**, and I am submitting it using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form (available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals) to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, with a copy sent by fax to **859-425-3379**. I can be reached by phone at the number above, and Aetna's member line is 1-800-872-3862.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this. I am trying to get back to sleeping through the night and climbing my own stairs.

Sincerely,

**Rowan Carter**
Member ID: W914903090
Reference number: POC-5BA41AD17E-24277

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated August 19, 2026
- MRI report dated June 9, 2026
- Physical therapy discharge note (April 10, 2026 – July 17, 2026, 16 visits)
- Office notes from Dr. Marchetti, orthopedic surgery
- Medication and injection records
- [Any additional records from my surgeon's office]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
